lines.raw: Mid cycle.
lines.say: Mid cycle.

lines.raw: The **mid cycle** turns the care given into **charges** (what was done, at the provider's price) and **codes** (what was done and why, in standard language), backed by the doctor's **documentation**.
lines.say: The mid cycle turns the care given into charges (what was done, at the provider's price) and codes (what was done and why, in standard language), backed by the doctor's documentation.

lines.raw: In the US: The mid cycle in the US.
lines.say: In the U S: The mid cycle in the U S.

lines.raw: **Charge capture**: every billable service is recorded, usually by the doctor or nurse clicking it in the electronic health record (EHR).
lines.say: Charge capture: every billable service is recorded, usually by the doctor or nurse clicking it in the electronic health record (E H R).

lines.raw: Each service is priced from the provider's **chargemaster**, its master price list.
lines.say: Each service is priced from the provider's chargemaster, its master price list.

lines.raw: The doctor writes a **clinical note**.
lines.say: The doctor writes a clinical note.

lines.raw: **Medical coders** (or the doctor, in many small clinics) turn the note into diagnosis and procedure codes.
lines.say: Medical coders (or the doctor, in many small clinics) turn the note into diagnosis and procedure codes.

lines.raw: Large hospitals have **clinical documentation integrity (CDI)** specialists who check notes are complete and specific enough to support the codes.
lines.say: Large hospitals have clinical documentation integrity (C D I) specialists who check notes are complete and specific enough to support the codes.

lines.raw: The **chargemaster** (also called the **charge description master**, or **CDM**) is the provider's list of every item it can bill, with a price.
lines.say: The chargemaster (also called the charge description master, or C D M) is the provider's list of every item it can bill, with a price.

lines.raw: How those list prices compare with what insurers actually pay is taught in the **Fee For Service** course.
lines.say: How those list prices compare with what insurers actually pay is taught in the Fee For Service course.

lines.raw: For RCM, the chargemaster matters as a **tool**: each line carries the codes that end up on the claim, so one wrong line causes errors on every claim that uses it.
lines.say: For R C M, the chargemaster matters as a tool: each line carries the codes that end up on the claim, so one wrong line causes errors on every claim that uses it.

lines.say: C P T (Current Procedural Terminology) codes describe services; H C P C S (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) adds supplies, drugs and some services.

lines.raw: A claim must say **why** care was given (diagnosis codes, from ICD-10-CM, the International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, Clinical Modification) and **what** was done (procedure codes, CPT or HCPCS).
lines.say: A claim must say why care was given (diagnosis codes, from I C D 10-CM, the International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, Clinical Modification) and what was done (procedure codes, C P T or H C P C S).

lines.raw: Coders can only code what the note supports.
lines.say: Coders can only code what the note supports.

lines.raw: If the note is vague, the codes are vague, and the insurer may pay less or deny.

lines.raw: Common mid-cycle problems.
lines.say: Common mid-cycle problems.

lines.raw: **Missed charge**. Example: A test was done but never clicked in the EHR. Effect: Lost revenue; nobody ever bills it.
lines.say: Missed charge. Example: A test was done but never clicked in the E H R. Effect: Lost revenue; nobody ever bills it.

lines.raw: **Wrong charge**. Example: Charged twice, or charged for a test that was cancelled. Effect: Overbilling; may lead to refunds or audits.
lines.say: Wrong charge. Example: Charged twice, or charged for a test that was cancelled. Effect: Overbilling; may lead to refunds or audits.

lines.raw: **Out-of-date chargemaster line**. Example: A code was deleted this year but the line still uses it. Effect: Every claim with that line is rejected.
lines.say: Out-of-date chargemaster line. Example: A code was deleted this year but the line still uses it. Effect: Every claim with that line is rejected.

lines.raw: **Weak documentation**. Example: The note does not say how complex the visit was. Effect: The visit level cannot be supported; may be paid lower or denied.
lines.say: Weak documentation. Example: The note does not say how complex the visit was. Effect: The visit level cannot be supported; may be paid lower or denied.

lines.raw: **Coding backlog**. Example: Charts wait days for a coder. Effect: Claims leave late; cash arrives late.
lines.say: Coding backlog. Example: Charts wait days for a coder. Effect: Claims leave late; cash arrives late.

lines.raw: The number of days from the **service date** to the date the charge is entered.

lines.raw: Charge lag (days) equals Charge entry date − Service date.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: The mid cycle turns care into **charges** (at chargemaster prices) and **codes** (ICD-10-CM, CPT/HCPCS), backed by documentation.
lines.say: The mid cycle turns care into charges (at chargemaster prices) and codes (I C D 10-CM, CPT/HCPCS), backed by documentation.

lines.raw: The **chargemaster** is the provider's master price list; each line carries the codes that flow onto claims.
lines.say: The chargemaster is the provider's master price list; each line carries the codes that flow onto claims.

lines.raw: Codes are only as good as the doctor's note; vague notes lead to lower payment or denials.
lines.say: Codes are only as good as the doctor's note; vague notes lead to lower payment or denials.

lines.raw: **Charge reconciliation** finds missed charges; **charge lag** measures how quickly charges are entered.
